standards.name: EDAM ontology (Data management branch)
standards.notes: Primary controlled vocabulary. Open OWL ontology with permanent per-term URIs. Browse: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/edam - Download: http://edamontology.org/EDAM.owl

standards.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
standards.notes: Optional secondary axis: the seven trustworthy-AI characteristics. Document-based, so individual characteristics have no per-term URIs. WARNING: NIST's 'Fair (harmful bias managed)' concerns algorithmic non-discrimination and is UNRELATED to EDAM's 'FAIR data' (Findable / Accessible / Interoperable / Reusable data principles) despite sharing the word - do not conflate the two. Also defines an AI lifecycle with named stages (plan, collect/process, build, verify, deploy, operate) -- cited here as e.g. "AI lifecycle stage: Deploy", distinct from the seven trustworthy-AI characteristics.

standards.name: ACM Computing Classification System (CCS 2012)
standards.notes: Cited by category path text (e.g. "Computer systems organization~Architectures"), not a numeric ID a human needs to look up -- confirmed against real paper citations. General computing/software-engineering taxonomy, not agentic-AI-specific -- predates MCP, agent frameworks, and tool-calling entirely, so it backs general CS terms (Architecture, Security, Evaluation, Retrieval) but not agent-specific ones (MCP, Hooks, Skills, Orchestration, ...). Path spellings below are from established domain knowledge, not a live verified fetch (dl.acm.org blocked automated access) -- worth spot-checking in a browser before treating as fully authoritative.

standards.name: Schema.org (CreativeWork hierarchy)
standards.notes: Universal web-metadata vocabulary. Exact-type matches applied directly (e.g. APIReference, BlogPosting, ScholarlyArticle, SoftwareSourceCode, Dataset). For highly specific AI-radar terms with no exact schema.org type, the broader parent type is applied instead (e.g. several terms map to TechArticle) -- this is schema.org's own intended usage pattern (broad type + a custom category property), not a forced fit, but it means several distinct Resource Type terms intentionally share one Ontology ID here, unlike EDAM/ACM-CCS/NIST-AI-RMF where each backed term has its own distinct match.

columns.name: Resource Name
columns.description: Short, human-readable name. Also the natural key used to match a row across sync runs. Example: VS Code Copilot Agents Overview

columns.name: Source Organization
columns.description: Who maintains it? Examples: Microsoft, GitHub, OpenAI, Kaggle, Anthropic, Google, HuggingFace. This matters because some orgs update weekly, others yearly.

columns.name: Last Verified
columns.description: Date a curator last checked the page. Set by a human during verification; cleared automatically when the row's content changes.

columns.name: Verified By
columns.description: Curator who last verified this row. Set by a human only, never by an agent; cleared automatically when the row's content changes.

columns.name: Last Updated
columns.description: The page's own update timestamp. Helps track fast-moving agent ecosystems.

columns.name: Deprecation Date
columns.description: Date the resource was deprecated or superseded.

columns.name: Version
columns.description: Version string of the resource or tool (e.g. 'v0.1 DRAFT', 'Pro'). Leave blank for article-type resources with no version - use Publication Date instead.

columns.name: Resource Type
columns.description: What kind of resource this is. Helps teams filter by what they need.

terms.name: Whitepaper
terms.definition: Vendor or organization technical whitepaper.

terms.name: Scientific Literature
terms.definition: Peer-reviewed publication or preprint. Distinct from a vendor Whitepaper.

terms.name: Benchmark Collection
terms.definition: A curated collection of benchmarks or comparison studies.

columns.name: Agentic Features Covered
columns.description: Which agentic capabilities the resource covers. One of the most important columns.

terms.name: MCP
terms.definition: Model Context Protocol.

terms.name: Evaluation / testing
terms.ontology_id: Software and its engineering~Software verification and validation~Software testing and debugging

terms.name: FAIR data
terms.definition: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable data principles.

columns.name: Topic Focus
columns.description: Subject areas the resource addresses. Helps research IT teams quickly find relevant material. Primary vocabulary is EDAM; NIST AI RMF characteristics are available as an optional secondary axis.

terms.name: Data governance
terms.definition: Focuses specifically on the technical protocols, access controls, data-line security, and de-identification standards used to protect the integrity, quality, and privacy of information throughout its lifecycle

terms.name: Governance
terms.definition: The overarching organizational policies, compliance frameworks, and capital allocation strategies that dictate how an enterprise manages its broader IT infrastructure, risk tolerances, and vendor choices

terms.name: Implementation
terms.ontology_id: Software and its engineering~Software creation and management

terms.name: Deployment
terms.definition: The tactical, hands-on execution of installing, configuring, provisioning, and launching software or hardware systems within a specific operational environment

terms.name: Evaluation
terms.ontology_id: Software and its engineering~Software verification and validation~Software testing and debugging

terms.name: Compute Infrastructure
terms.definition: Physical node topologies, hardware constraints, VRAM bounds, and localized compute execution profiles.

terms.name: Network Isolation
terms.definition: Non-egress boundaries, air-gapped artifact staging, localized cloud VPC containers, and firewalled local registries.

terms.name: Infrastructure Security
terms.definition: For on-prem LLM deployments, it captures the security of the compute stack as well as the data pipelines

terms.name: Self‑hosted AI
terms.definition: Self‑hosted, open‑weights models in contrast to API‑based models like OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini

terms.name: Data Protection
terms.definition: Safeguarding sensitive data specifically. Distinct from the broader Security term.

terms.name: FAIR data
terms.definition: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable data principles.

terms.name: Valid and Reliable
terms.definition: NIST AI RMF trustworthy-AI characteristic.

terms.name: Safe
terms.definition: NIST AI RMF trustworthy-AI characteristic.

terms.name: Secure and Resilient
terms.definition: NIST AI RMF trustworthy-AI characteristic.

terms.name: Accountable and Transparent
terms.definition: NIST AI RMF trustworthy-AI characteristic.

terms.name: Explainable and Interpretable
terms.definition: NIST AI RMF trustworthy-AI characteristic.

terms.name: Privacy-Enhanced
terms.definition: NIST AI RMF trustworthy-AI characteristic.

terms.name: Fair (harmful bias managed)
terms.definition: NIST AI RMF trustworthy-AI characteristic: algorithmic non-discrimination. NOT the same as 'FAIR data'.

columns.name: Relevance to Research Cyberinfrastructure
columns.description: Free-text note on why this matters to research platforms. Example themes: workflow orchestration, data portal integration, metadata / provenance, multi-agent coordination, HPC / cloud hybrid workflows, reproducibility, federated analysis, user-facing agent interfaces.

columns.name: Maturity Level
columns.description: Not about the website - about the technology described. Helps teams know whether something is stable enough to consider.

columns.name: Notes / Key Takeaways
columns.description: Short free-text field: breaking changes, important patterns, new capabilities, relevance to agentic workflows, implications for research platforms. This is where institutional knowledge accumulates.

columns.name: Publication Date
columns.description: Publication date for article-type resources that have no software version.

columns.name: Discovery Date
columns.description: Date this resource first entered the VT Radar.
